persona: Same field biologist's forest-inventory collaborator, running fixed-area tree plots for a stand-structure survey
source_style: exported from R with write.csv(df, file, row.names=FALSE) after entering plot tallies into a data frame

columns.name: tree_id
columns.notes: integer, renumbered 1..n within each plot (not globally unique)

columns.name: species_code
columns.notes: USDA-style 4-letter species code; SPECIES_NAMES map: ACSA=Acer saccharum, QURU=Quercus rubra, BEPA=Betula papyrifera, PIST=Pinus strobus, FAGR=Fagus grandifolia, TSCA=Tsuga canadensis

columns.name: dbh_cm
columns.notes: diameter at breast height, cm, 1 decimal, species-specific realistic range

columns.name: height_m
columns.notes: total height, m, 1 decimal; correlated with dbh (height = 1.3 + 0.35*dbh + noise), floor of 3.0

columns.name: decay_class
columns.notes: 1 (recently dead) to 5 (highly decayed) snag decay class; only scored for dead trees. R's write.csv prints the literal unquoted text 'NA' for alive trees' missing value, not a blank cell

columns.name: date_measured
columns.notes: ISO yyyy-mm-dd, one date per plot (all trees in a plot measured the same field day)

clean_table.generation_rule: One row per tree, grouped by plot in the fixed order P01 (2024-07-08), P02 (2024-07-08), P03 (2024-07-09), P04 (2024-07-10). Per plot, n_trees = rng.randint(10,15), then tree_id runs 1..n_trees. Each tree draws species_code via rng.choices(['ACSA','QURU','BEPA','PIST','FAGR','TSCA'], weights=[0.28,0.22,0.15,0.12,0.15,0.08]). dbh_cm = round(rng.uniform(lo,hi),1) where (lo,hi) is the species' range: ACSA(15,45), QURU(20,55), BEPA(8,25), PIST(25,60), FAGR(10,35), TSCA(15,40). height_m = round(1.3 + 0.35*dbh_cm + rng.uniform(-2,2), 1), floored at 3.0. status='alive' if rng.random()<0.85 else 'dead'. decay_class = the literal string 'NA' if alive, else rng.randint(1,5). All randomness from random.Random(7), consumed per tree in order: species_code, dbh, height, alive-roll, decay (if dead), looping trees within each plot, plots in the fixed order above.

intended_analysis: Does mean tree diameter (or species composition, or the proportion of standing dead trees) differ among the 4 plots? Also used to fit a simple height-diameter allometric relationship across species.
what_a_naive_reader_would_get_wrong: Reading decay_class as a numeric column and choking on (or silently coercing) the literal text 'NA' for every alive tree, rather than recognizing it as R's missing-value marker for a variable that is structurally undefined (not just unmeasured) when status='alive'.
